name: FleetDB
tagline: Schema-free in-memory document database in Clojure with a JSON query protocol and append-only log durability.
description: FleetDB is a schema-free document database written in Clojure by Mark McGranaghan, which grew out of his senior thesis at Bowdoin College in 2009-2010. All data is held in memory as Clojure persistent data structures, every write is appended to a log that is replayed on start-up and can be compacted or snapshotted, and clients send queries as JSON arrays over a plain TCP socket, or call it in-process via an embedded API. The query set covers select with where, order, limit, offset and distinct, plus insert, update, delete, count, explain, index creation and atomic multi-read, multi-write and checked-write operations, with optional password authentication. The last release, 0.3.1, came out in September 2010, and the README now says the project is no longer active.
statusNote: The author marks it as no longer active; last release 0.3.1 (September 2010).
strengths: Clean, small Clojure codebase showing an immutable in-memory database with log replay
Readable JSON query protocol with explain, indexes and atomic multi-query operations
Embeddable in-process or usable as a TCP server
weaknesses: Inactive since 2010 and tied to Clojure 1.2-era dependencies
Whole dataset must fit in memory
useCases: Studying how persistent data structures can back a database
Teaching examples of log-structured durability and query planning
